races.name: L & R Pest Control Services Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Iain Jardine who finished second on Good going last time out 8 days ago; gets a soft lead here with no obvious challenger for the early rail, but the prominent tag and STYLE_FIT flag suggest his chance diminishes in scenarios where he is pushed into a harder race.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for the same Jardine yard, with two placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs; the 14-day return (2F flag noted) needs monitoring but on Good ground at 2m with a conditional claiming 3lb, a truly-run race where he can produce a late run is his only realistic winning shape.

runners_data.name: Betteryouthanme
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing mare with a Good-ground win over 2m on her card (1/16f/GOO) and in decent recent form — a third and a first in last five; William Maggs takes the ride and she is the most likely horse to secure a genuine prominent position behind Newport, making her well-placed whatever the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type for Sandy Thomson, fitted with a p-plate and last seen finishing seventh over 21f on Good; three placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs but 28 days off and the 7lb claimer Walkingshaw could be a concern in a tactical race.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been running almost exclusively on Soft ground (five of last five in hist), yet is shown as OK for Good today; the 110-day break is a significant fitness question, and Mark Walford's 0/18 in the last 14 days does nothing to encourage confidence, despite the two second-place finishes last season.

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: Prominent type for David Thompson wearing first-time p-plate, returning from 44 days (19F flag noted after a fall); best form has come on Soft (1/20f/SOF) and his 11 similar-going runs have only produced 1 win and 4 places, so Good ground is a slight uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Snapaudaciaheros
runners_data.note: Two wins from 14 similar-going runs and in excellent recent form — P and 1 in last two — but this horse's natural prominence means it has been pushed back on the map as the field is too front-heavy; Rebecca Menzies sends it back 8 days after a win and Charlie Maggs rides, though finding a comfortable position early will be the key challenge.

runners_data.name: Curious Mrs Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for David Thompson who has run six times and is yet to win, with a best of third; Hexham's tight 2m over Good with a claimer riding does not immediately suggest she can break her duck, and the form line of 43-66 lacks recent encouragement.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (2W4P from 15 similar-going runs) but at 11 years old this is a horse whose natural race rhythm as a prominent runner is disrupted here — squeezed out of position by the density of prominent types in front of him; Jack Stenhouse (7lb) claims, and trainer Harrison has 0/4 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Knockeranna Rose
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare mapped to midfield because the rear is also congested; has placed four times from 11 similar-going runs and finished second over 2m Good at Hexham before, giving her course-and-distance form, though the 39-day absence for Susan Corbett's yard (0/11 in 14 days) tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Bouboule
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type wearing first-time tp, last seen finishing seventh 14 days ago (3F flag noted); the entire form profile reads 355P-7 with no wins from 15 similar-going runs, and as a young horse forced into a race with compressed positions and a lightly-experienced 7lb claimer aboard, this is a significant ask.

races.paceDynamic: Newport is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead, looks set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Hexham's tight circuit over 2m on Good ground. Behind him, Betteryouthanme, Huit Reflets, and Top Flight Century will seek the prominent positions, while Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen are genuine prominent types who are effectively squeezed out of their natural berths by the volume of horses wanting to race close to the pace — both are likely to find themselves racing slightly further back than ideal. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position, with Newport best-placed to take the lead and Betteryouthanme the most likely to lock in a genuine prominent spot; Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen will have to settle for a less comfortable role. A single unhurried pace-setter on Good ground at Hexham sets up a race that will favour horses who can travel prominently in the first two or three and then sustain their effort into the home straight — patient closers attempting a late run will face a track that does not easily reward sweeping finishes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Newport Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Newport leads unchallenged and the pace is steady enough that the prominent horses travelling just behind him can strike approaching the final flight.
scenarios.body: If Newport leads unchallenged and the pace is steady enough that the prominent horses travelling just behind him can strike approaching the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Newport's uncontested lead tempts him into going too slowly and the race bunches, allowing a late flourish from horses held up off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Newport's uncontested lead tempts him into going too slowly and the race bunches, allowing a late flourish from horses held up off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Crowding Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen push forward harder than expected and Newport is unable to lead unchallenged, forcing a more contentious early pace.
scenarios.body: If Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen push forward harder than expected and Newport is unable to lead unchallenged, forcing a more contentious early pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Outclassed
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuine clip from the front and the hold-up horses simply cannot land a telling blow from their position in a small-ish field.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at a genuine clip from the front and the hold-up horses simply cannot land a telling blow from their position in a small-ish field.

watchPoints.text: Newport (front-runner) sets the entire complexion of this race — if he gets a soft lead and travels kindly, he controls the tempo and threatens to make this a procession for those immediately behind him; watch for whether Betteryouthanme or Snapaudaciaheros press him in the early stages.

Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen are both genuine prominent types who cannot both hold their natural position — watch for a tactical scramble in the first half-mile as they attempt to slot in closer to Newport than the map suggests, which could compromise their jumping rhythm.

Huit Reflets returns from a 110-day absence with a Going concern (all recent form on Soft) — if the Good ground rides quicker than expected, his jumping sharpness after a long absence becomes a jumping safety concern as much as a performance one.

The 3F flag on Mr Lincoln (Iain Jardine) and the 2F flag on Bouboule (Gillian Boanas) are worth monitoring in the paddock — fitness queries in a conditional jockeys' handicap can be amplified by less experienced riders if a horse is not fully wound up.

Top Flight Century carries a 19F flag (fall on last run 44 days ago) and is fitted with first-time headgear — his jumping confidence and how he travels through the first few flights on the undulating Hexham track is a key early race indicator.

races.name: Chris Lowther & Brian Ellison 28 Years Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Beyond The Verge
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with a win on Good ground at 2m and solid Corbett stable form; 435 days off the track is a significant concern over this trip, though the style suits and Moscrop is a capable claiming pilot.

runners_data.name: Getaway Vic
runners_data.note: Shane Fenelon (5lb claim) takes the ride and this mare boasts six runs on Good ground with two wins and five places — the most consistent similar-going record in the field; the 2-day turnaround is worth monitoring but connections clearly believe she's ready.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rocco
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and returning after 353 days, with a form string of falls and a sole comparable-going run finishing sixth; tongue-tie is fitted and Patrick Neville's yard has been quiet, making this a speculative entry at best.

runners_data.name: Teofimo
runners_data.note: His true style is hold-up but the race shape leaves him unable to settle far off the pace as he'd prefer; five of his eight career runs on comparable ground produced finishes of sixth or worse, and 343 days off the track adds to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Run Happy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced juvenile type returning after just 12 days for a yard in strong form (Easterby, 5/39 over 14 days); only two comparable-going runs offer limited evidence, and his best placed finish came over a shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: Returns after 14 days for Patrick Neville and her natural inclination to race from the back is compromised by the field's configuration — her three Good-ground runs produced no better than fourth; the trip may suit but she needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: Derek Fox, a highly experienced northern rider, partners this seven-year-old who has shown nothing better than fifth from one comparable-going run; a poor recent form string (P354-7) offers little encouragement even if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's home hope — the trainer connection is noted but two successive sixths on Good ground over shorter tell a flat story; the step up to 2m4f is unexplored and there is no evidence yet of the gears needed to compete here.

runners_data.name: Loman Lady
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton combine with this five-year-old who has won on Good over 2m, making her the structural pace-setter for this race; her recent win 8 days ago suggests peak fitness, though the style-fit tag means rivals will target her late.

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: A hurdling headgear (p) runner who placed at 3m on Good ground last time, suggesting the longer test suits; Jamie Hamilton's local knowledge is an asset and the recent form is honest enough to make her a live midfield finisher.

runners_data.name: Rachel Lopez
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan takes this hold-up performer who has two placed runs on comparable ground including a second on Soft; her Hexham experience from similar northern tracks and consistent placed form give her a credible each-way profile in a scenario that sees the leaders come back.

races.paceDynamic: Loman Lady (Harry Skelton, Dan Skelton) is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, she should dictate an unhurried, controlled gallop over this 2m4f Hexham trip on Good ground. Beyond The Verge and Getaway Vic will look to press from prominent positions, creating a small lead group, but the overall tempo is unlikely to be severe enough to crack the field apart early. This shapes as a race where the front-running profile is dominant — a horse who can lead or sit just off the pace, conserve energy on the undulations, and quicken on the run-in holds the clearest structural advantage. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically be placed at the rear — Dolly Dior and Teofimo are genuine closers by nature but have been mapped to midfield because the rear is crowded; neither is likely to get the deep rearward pitch that suits them best, which marginalises their chances in a slowly-run scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loman Lady Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Loman Lady bowls along unchallenged and sets a sustainable pace that stretches the field on the final circuit.
scenarios.body: If Loman Lady bowls along unchallenged and sets a sustainable pace that stretches the field on the final circuit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Beyond The Verge or Getaway Vic push forward hard early and force a stronger pace that reorders the front group.
scenarios.body: If Beyond The Verge or Getaway Vic push forward hard early and force a stronger pace that reorders the front group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is hot enough to soften the leaders and a well-positioned midfield horse arrives late with a decisive run.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is hot enough to soften the leaders and a well-positioned midfield horse arrives late with a decisive run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running group falls apart through jumping errors or a collapse in tempo that leaves a complete outsider in front.
scenarios.body: If the front-running group falls apart through jumping errors or a collapse in tempo that leaves a complete outsider in front.

watchPoints.text: Loman Lady's jumping under pressure — if she makes an error at a critical hurdle mid-race, her advantage evaporates instantly and Beyond The Verge or Getaway Vic are positioned to inherit.

Getaway Vic's 2-day turnaround is unusually quick and connections should be watched at the start for any signs of over-freshness or a tardy jump that costs her the prominent position her form demands.
Redbridge Rocco and Teofimo both return from layoffs exceeding 340 days — either horse could jump poorly or fade quickly if fitness is short, creating interference risk in a maiden hurdle field.
Beyond The Verge's 435-day absence means her jumping sharpness over the Hexham fences is genuinely unknown; a single error could see her lose the prominent pitch she needs to be competitive.

The Hexham undulations and downhill sections favour horses with clean jumping technique — monitor Frisky Whiskey and Run Happy early, as neither has shown form suggesting they handle varied terrain comfortably.

races.name: Matfen Hall Hotel Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Parisencore
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader who can dictate from the front; Danny McMenamin is a strong tactical jockey at Hexham, and the horse's two wins in five similar-going runs this season show he is effective when controlling the tempo, though he has finished fourth in four of his last five and a 10-year-old may lack the finishing kick if pressed from the home turn.

runners_data.name: Cossack Chach
runners_data.note: Returning from a 211-day layoff which is the primary risk factor; showed a win over this sort of trip on good ground before his break and the headgear (tongue-piece) may sharpen focus on reappearance, but the ring-rust concern is real and Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore's 1-from-16 trainer form over 14 days adds to the caution.

runners_data.name: Kientzheim
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for Ben Haslam, a powerful combination, and the horse has finished first or second in three of his last four on ground similar to today's; tracks the pace naturally, which suits the expected race shape perfectly, and the step down from 20f last time to 1m7½f today looks a positive adjustment.

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Sam England's 10-year-old won most recently and is back quickly after just 15 days, with blinkers and tongue-tie in place to maintain intensity; a genuine hold-up horse by style who needs the pace to be honest — he is perfectly placed if the front-runners overshoot, but this controlled tempo may not generate enough late drama for him to pounce.

runners_data.name: Cobbler's Boy
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton combine with a 6-year-old who has won twice in his last five and goes well on good ground; hold-up in style but showed a win over 16f on good going recently, and the yard's 15-from-32 trainer form at 14 days gives confidence he arrives ready to perform — needs the pace to set things up from the rear.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Patrick Griffin's 6-year-old is a front-running type in its natural inclinations but, with Parisencore already committed to the lead, is likely to find itself shuffled into midfield rather than its preferred position; Brian Hughes is an excellent pilot who can adapt, and the horse's consistent placing record (three placed efforts in last five runs on similar going) suggests it will not be disgraced even racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Conquer The Breeze
runners_data.note: Back quickly after 15 days and has won twice in recent outings — on good and soft — giving it genuine live form; at heart a horse that wants to be prominent, and Adam Nicol's 1-from-8 trainer form over 14 days is modest, but the bigger issue tactically is that it is unlikely to secure its natural pressing position and must instead produce its effort from a less comfortable midfield berth.

races.paceDynamic: Parisencore is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to force a contested pace from the outset, Danny McMenamin can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m7½f trip on good ground at Hexham. Herja and Conquer The Breeze are both natural prominent-tracking types by profile but, with Parisencore already occupying that lead slot and the field containing more front-running intent than the race shape can accommodate, both are likely to find themselves racing in unfamiliar midfield positions rather than where they would naturally want to be. This creates a race run at a measured tempo with a single leader setting a comfortable rhythm, which historically at Hexham over this trip favours horses who can travel prominently just off the pace and produce a sustained gallop from the home turn rather than a late burst from off the bridle. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent-to-lead profiles who can settle within striking distance of Parisencore without over-committing early hold the structural advantage, while true hold-up horses will need the pace to collapse to get into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore bowls along uncontested at a fair but unhurried clip and the winner strikes from close proximity turning in.
scenarios.body: If Parisencore bowls along uncontested at a fair but unhurried clip and the winner strikes from close proximity turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore's controlled gallop is slow enough that he builds a lead no rival can close down in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Parisencore's controlled gallop is slow enough that he builds a lead no rival can close down in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from the back of the final circuit and the leaders empty inside the last two fences.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens sharply from the back of the final circuit and the leaders empty inside the last two fences.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Herja or Conquer The Breeze push forward from their expected midfield positions and inject genuine pace to challenge Parisencore early.
scenarios.body: If Herja or Conquer The Breeze push forward from their expected midfield positions and inject genuine pace to challenge Parisencore early.

watchPoints.text: Cossack Chach returns from 211 days off — watch the paddock and early race behaviour closely, as a fresh horse can either bounce off a layoff or show ring-rust that compounds a poor starting position.

Herja and Conquer The Breeze may push forward early to reclaim their natural prominent ground — if either forces a contested pace against Parisencore, the tempo will be faster than the race shape suggests and the dynamics shift sharply against hold-up horses.

Parisencore's STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder this horse is technically being asked to lead rather than track — McMenamin may need to adjust if the horse does not settle in front, which could create a false gallop and compress the field earlier than expected.

Glory And Honour runs just 15 days after its last outing and carries blinkers and tongue-tie — watch whether the stable has freshened it sufficiently or whether the quick turnaround dulls its finishing effort in the straight.

Hexham's home straight is short and the final fence comes up quickly — horses that have travelled well in the first half of the race are disproportionately advantaged here, making early positioning behind Parisencore a critical factor to monitor from the start.

races.name: Jethro's Cafe Of Haltwhistle Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Perseus Way
runners_data.note: In career-best form with three consecutive wins, all on Good or Soft ground at 2m-plus, and arrives fresh on just 8 days' turnaround — a hold-up horse whose finishing kick is well-suited to the controlled pace High Dancer is likely to set; Good ground is clearly its medium and the sharp Hexham track should not inconvenience it.

runners_data.name: High Dancer
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here under Danny McMenamin for Nicky Richards, whose 1/5 T14 strike rate is respectable, but racing from a prominent position is effectively its natural role and it faces minimal early pressure with only four rivals — the key question is whether it has enough in the tank after 24 days off to hold on when challenged late.

runners_data.name: Haarar
runners_data.note: Sam England's runner returns after an 82-day absence (34 days filtered flag) with all five recent runs on Soft ground, making this Good surface a potential unknown; its best form has come prominently ridden but it will need to show sharp freshness to justify support given the layoff and the absence of any comparable going wins in its recent history.

runners_data.name: Winds Of Winter
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by inclination whose spot in the map is a consequence of too many front-end types in this field — Conor Rabbitt (3) takes over for George Bewley, whose yard has had a quiet 14 days (0/6), and its best chance depends on working closer to the pace than the race shape readily permits; STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: A model of consistency without a win from its last ten — George Bewley's second runner here is a true hold-up horse whose five-run placed sequence on Good ground over 2m shows it stays on reliably; the 8-day turnaround is fine, but its inability to win from this profile when the opportunity presents keeps its win probability modest.

races.paceDynamic: High Dancer is the confirmed front runner and, with only five runners over 2m at Hexham on Good ground, should secure an uncontested lead from the outset and dictate a sustainable, measured gallop throughout. Haarar and Winds Of Winter are both natural prominent types, but with High Dancer already filling that slot, at least one of them will be shuffled back from their preferred position — the field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, with High Dancer and Haarar most likely to secure the early positions and Winds Of Winter the one most likely to be displaced rearward. Perseus Way and Well Educated are genuine hold-up horses who will settle in behind and rely on their finishing efforts, though Perseus Way's recent hat-trick of wins gives it the most potent late threat. A controlled, single-pace gallop over this sharp 2m trip favours the closers who can produce a clean late challenge — specifically hold-up horses with proven form on Good ground and the resolution to pick off a front runner who has not been pressured — making Perseus Way the primary beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If High Dancer sets an uncontested, honest but sustainable gallop and the hold-up horses land a clean run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If High Dancer sets an uncontested, honest but sustainable gallop and the hold-up horses land a clean run from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays modest enough that Haarar or High Dancer have enough in reserve to resist the closers to the line.
scenarios.body: If the pace stays modest enough that Haarar or High Dancer have enough in reserve to resist the closers to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If High Dancer sets a frantic early pace that burns itself out before two out, opening the race up for a sweeping finish.
scenarios.body: If High Dancer sets a frantic early pace that burns itself out before two out, opening the race up for a sweeping finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Winds Of Winter, despite being displaced from its natural prominent position, recovers mid-race and delivers a timely challenge.
scenarios.body: If Winds Of Winter, despite being displaced from its natural prominent position, recovers mid-race and delivers a timely challenge.

watchPoints.text: Perseus Way's three-timer run on Good ground makes it the most dangerous hold-up threat — watch for Harry Reed to time the challenge from off the pace as High Dancer comes back to the field in the straight.

Haarar's 82-day absence and all-Soft recent form creates a fitness and going unknown — if it is not fully wound up, it could drop away sharply after the second-last and open gaps for the closers behind it.

Winds Of Winter is a natural prominent racer and Conor Rabbitt may push it forward early regardless of the race map — if it does compete for position with High Dancer and Haarar, the early tempo could be materially faster than the pace map suggests, changing the shape of the race.

Well Educated's consistency at 2m on Good ground for a trainer with a quiet recent record (0/6 T14) means it is unlikely to win but almost certain to make the frame — it sets a useful benchmark for the placed positions behind the likely winner.

With only five runners and a lone confirmed front runner, Hexham's tight turning track means positioning over the first few flights will be unusually decisive — any horse that loses its pitch early will face a tough task regaining ground on a circuit that does not provide long straight recovery time.

races.name: Tynedale Function Suite Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ostend
runners_data.note: Has been consistent at this grade with recent form reading /334-2 and handles Good ground well (6 runs, 2 wins/4 places on similar going); confirmed front-runner whose chance hinges on jumping fluently and fending off Passengerontheship — the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence if forced off its lead.|

runners_data.name: Buddah Castle
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes booking is significant and the horse won last time out over 2m4f on soft; only three runs on similar going so the sample is thin, but Good ground here is not a concern and the 94-day absence is the key question mark with trainer T14 rate at 0/7.|

runners_data.name: Moodofthemoment
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong course-form footprint (11 runs, 3W/4P on similar going) and headgear retained; the 9-year-old has bounced back from defeats before and this Good ground/2m4f combo is exactly the scenario in which this horse posts its best figures.|

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes over for the Skelton yard firing at 15/32 in the last 14 days — a compelling trainer-jockey combination; the 5-year-old has run consistently without winning (0 wins from 7 on similar going) but the form string shows progressive placing and this drop in OR to 101 looks attractive.|

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Three wins from the last four starts is a red-hot sequence and the horse handles Good ground over this trip expertly; headgear is retained, Sam England's yard is ticking over at 4/15 T14, and the recent 8-day turnaround is worth monitoring though the horse clearly thrives with racing.|

runners_data.name: West Lawn
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent in style but cannot get that position here with Ostend and Passengerontheship ahead of it in the pecking order, so it is effectively racing out of role; the OR of 84 leaves it with most to find against the principals even if it finds an ideal pitch, and the Walton yard is 0/1 in the past 14 days.|

races.paceDynamic: Ostend is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Passengerontheship as a genuine rival for prominent pitch, should be able to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without being seriously challenged for the lead. Passengerontheship has won three of its last four and will want to race prominently, so Ostend will not be entirely alone on the front end, but neither horse figures to ignite a truly searching pace on Good ground over 2m4f. West Lawn is a natural prominent racer who cannot get that position in this shape and has been mapped to midfield as a consequence — the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural berths, with Ostend and Passengerontheship most likely to lock out the front rank. The resulting race shape — a controlled, single-file lead from Ostend at a fair but unspectacular tempo — strongly favours hold-up and late-travelling types who can track the pace comfortably and produce a clean round of jumping, particularly Moodofthemoment and Laffer Curve, both of whom have the profiles to benefit from a well-run but not gruelling gallop on ground that suits them.

scenarios.title: Ostend Controls, Closers Strike

scenarios.body: If Ostend dictates from the front at a fair pace and no rival has the firepower to disrupt the tempo.

scenarios.title: Passengerontheship Presses On
scenarios.trigger: If Passengerontheship pushes up to challenge Ostend early and the two front horses set a genuinely contested pace.
scenarios.body: If Passengerontheship pushes up to challenge Ostend early and the two front horses set a genuinely contested pace.

scenarios.title: Passengerontheship Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Passengerontheship is allowed to stride on and Ostend is ridden more conservatively than expected.
scenarios.body: If Passengerontheship is allowed to stride on and Ostend is ridden more conservatively than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: West Lawn Finds Position, Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If West Lawn manages to slot into a prominent berth against its mapped position and the pace collapses in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: If West Lawn manages to slot into a prominent berth against its mapped position and the pace collapses in the final half-mile.

watchPoints.text: Passengerontheship's aggressive front-running instinct could push up against Ostend from the second fence — watch whether Jonathan England tests Ostend's lead or settles for second in the early exchanges, as that decision shapes the entire race tempo.

Moodofthemoment carries headgear and is noted as a hold-up type: if the pace is too steady and the field bunches, Ellis Collier (5lb claim) may find it difficult to manoeuvre through traffic at a crucial stage.
Buddah Castle returns after 94 days off with trainer Patrick Neville at 0/7 over the past fortnight — first-time back fitness is the single biggest threat to what looks a live form entry.

West Lawn has been redistributed to midfield but Charlie Maggs (3lb claim) may attempt to push forward from the outset; if it does secure a prominent pitch, the fencing ability and track-knowledge at Hexham (four recent runs here) becomes a minor plus worth tracking.

Laffer Curve's last two runs have both been over 2m (20f) on Good — this step up to 2m4f (20f to 20f in the form, but check — this is 20f in form vs 20f here) is a flat distance profile; Harry Skelton's judgement of pace on a left-handed track like Hexham will be pivotal in whether the horse gets a clean sight of the final fences.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here; Sam England's nine-year-old goes prominent as a matter of course and sim-going form (13/15 on Good) is strong — the key question is whether he can dictate alone over 2m7½f without eventually being reeled in by fresher rivals.

runners_data.name: Nitty Gritty
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Conor Rabbitt (3lb claimer) who has shown glimpses over 2m+ on Good but a modest sim-going record (0W1P) and the OR drop to 98 may not be enough to compensate for a lack of early pace; will need things to go wrong up front.

runners_data.name: Miss Kassiopi
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners the Skelton yard's consistent performer whose form figures of 2-2-1-3 at similar trips on Good ground give her strong credentials; naturally prominent-running and should secure a handy berth tracking Jeteye with a 15/32 T14 strike rate behind her.

runners_data.name: Stylish Recruit
runners_data.note: Sandy Thomson's eight-year-old carries OR 94 and has won twice on Good ground at 24f — blinkers/cheekpieces in place and Patrick Wadge aboard; genuinely prominent-running type who should slot in directly off Jeteye's pace and represents live each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Jimli's Cave
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on this Watson-trained hold-up horse fitted with a visor; sim-going record is excellent (14/15 on Good) and the eight-year-old stays well — ran only 8 days ago, which warrants monitoring for freshness but Hughes is a master at placing them late at Hexham.

runners_data.name: Belladinotte
runners_data.note: Won at 24f on Good ground for Sara Ender and Harry Bannister renews the partnership; naturally prominent-running with a 2W record at similar trips — the 19-day break looks straightforward and she is firmly in the mix if she can slot behind Jeteye early.

runners_data.name: Robert d'Ores
runners_data.note: George Bewley's nine-year-old has a poor sim-going record (0W1P from 7 runs) and consistent form figures of 4-6-6-7-6 suggest he is one to oppose; prominent runner who will likely sit in the pack without the finishing kick to challenge.

runners_data.name: Lady Phoebe
runners_data.note: Won at 22f on Good ground (OR 84) and Ryan Mania is an experienced handler at this track; however she is a natural front-runner who has been pushed back in the map — with several stronger prominent types ahead of her in the pecking order, she will struggle to get the race run to suit and her 82-day layoff (13 from last run flag) adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Star Vantage
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's nine-year-old is a hold-up type whose best form figures (4-4-4-5) come from sitting off the pace; sim-going record is modest (0W2P) and a 58-day break is notable — Jamie Hamilton will be patient but the horse needs the pace to collapse rather than just moderate to win.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan partners this Whillans-trained nine-year-old who is, in truth, a front-running type; pushed back to midfield in the map because the prominent berths are oversubscribed — his 3W career record was built racing handy and he will underperform if he cannot get to his natural position, so treat with caution despite an active strike rate for the yard.

runners_data.name: Twoplacesatonetime
runners_data.note: Nathan Moscrop rides the Menzies second string carrying a hood (hg:p); two pulled-ups in recent form (U-U) are worrying flags and sim-going record (1W1P from 7) offers little encouragement — distance experience is there but jumping reliability must be questioned.

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: Charlie Maggs (3lb claimer) partners Patrick Neville's mare who is a genuine hold-up horse; her true style is from the rear, though the map slots her to midfield given how many true closers this field contains — going record (12/14 on Good) is solid but a modest OR of 74 makes it hard to see her winning even if conditions suit perfectly.

runners_data.name: Dartmhor
runners_data.note: Chris Grant's six-year-old is a real hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity; a heavy-ground specialist (sim-going only 3/10 on Good) stepping into Good conditions for the first time in a while off 88 days, which is a significant concern — Danny McMenamin has the booking but the form figures (0W0P sim-going) and lack of recent sharpness make this a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Jeteye is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap hurdle over 2m7½f at Hexham, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Sam England's nine-year-old should bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground without ever being seriously pressured into going faster than suits. The field contains considerably more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Miss Kassiopi, Stylish Recruit, Belladinotte and Robert d'Ores are all natural front-rank horses and will press forward to contest a handful of spots directly behind Jeteye, compressing the early order and leaving redistributed types like Lady Phoebe and Luminaries racing further back than their profiles demand. Over this marathon trip on a track that tests stamina through Hexham's undulations, a controlled front-running display by Jeteye with a clutch of genuine prominents tracking closely is the dominant shape — and that profile overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel prominently with cover, conserving energy before the final climb, rather than those asking late questions from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Jeteye leads alone throughout — if no prominent rival is willing to go after him before the back straight, monitor whether he is building an unassailable lead that leaves the chasing pack with too much to do at the last.

The compression of prominent runners (Miss Kassiopi, Stylish Recruit, Belladinotte, Robert d'Ores) directly behind Jeteye creates a traffic-management risk at early hurdles — watch for interference or a false jump that shuffles the order dramatically.

Lady Phoebe and Luminaries are natural front-runners who cannot get their position in this field shape — if either of them makes an unexpected move for the lead in the first mile it could destabilise Jeteye's controlled tempo and trigger a faster early pace than anticipated.

Twoplacesatonetime has pulled up in two of its last five starts — Brian Hughes is not aboard and Nathan Moscrop's lighter experience at this level means jumping errors are a live risk over this marathon trip; be alert to the horse departing early and causing interference.

Dartmhor's 88-day absence combined with a poor sim-going record on Good ground (3/10) means Danny McMenamin may be instructed to give it an educational run — if so, the horse drifting wide or going slowly into hurdles at the back of the field could create a loose-horse concern late on.
